statusText: Green. The weekend CME halt continues with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail rests at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.

headline: Nasdaq-100: primary-source confirmation of the Jackson Hole repricing leaves tail risk at the low-band floor through the halt
body:
This assessment falls inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The anchor is Friday's completed session, re-verified against the Nasdaq-100 quote page this hour: the index opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.60 previous close. That leaves the close roughly 50 points off the low of a 369-point range, a downside reversal inside a finished session. The Nasdaq Composite ended 0.52% lower at 26,402.42 and the S&P 500 closed 7,711.76, down 0.25%, yet all three major indexes still posted a winning week. VIX closed 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 range and carried no volatility premium into the weekend.

The addition this hour is primary-source provenance for the catalyst. The Federal Reserve's published keynote text from the 2026 Jackson Hole symposium confirms the hawkish framing directly rather than through secondary reporting: 12-month PCE inflation at 3.7%, 54 percent of the PCE basket rising above 3 percent, and the explicit condition that if the Committee cannot be confident underlying inflation is moving to target at sufficient speed, 'we have work to do'. Reuters reported the market response as a roughly 11 basis point jump in the 2-year yield to about 4.34-4.35%, the 10-year up 5 basis points to 4.72% and the 30-year at 5.206%, with the implied probability of a September increase moving from about 35% to about 60%. H.15 carries the 2-year at 4.20% for 27 August, which frames the size of Friday's move. WTI closed 83.44, down 0.11%, as the Hormuz risk premium continued to unwind. Yields repriced sharply while oil and volatility stayed contained, which reads as repricing rather than a stress impulse.

The shared Finviz cross-asset context was healthy this hour at roughly 44 minutes old and was used as delayed supporting evidence only. It shows the latest-session split clearly: all seven tracked semiconductor names lower, led by ARM at -6.33% and NVDA at -4.57%, against gains in AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, META and GOOGL. Technology fell 1.41% while Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical rose. That is rotation inside the index rather than an aligned one-way move, and it is the clearest reading yet of why NDX fell while the Composite's week stayed positive. Treasury futures were lower across the curve, consistent with the verified cash move.

The week ahead is loaded but nothing lands inside the projected window. ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS both print Tuesday at 14:00 UTC, ADP follows Wednesday, Broadcom reports after Wednesday's close, and the August employment report lands Friday, the last major release before the 16 September policy decision. One structural detail applies to Monday itself: the London Stock Exchange is closed for the UK Summer Bank Holiday, so the European session will be continental-only and thinner than a normal Monday, and 31 August is also the final session of the month.

Tail therefore stays at the low-band floor of 5 and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Stress rises one point to 29 on the confirmed scale of the front-end repricing against a data-heavy week. Confidence rises to 85: current index levels, yields, oil, VIX, the primary catalyst text and the verified seven-day calendar are all in hand, and the shared cross-asset context is fresh again after being stale last hour. The single acknowledged gap remains the absence of any live price path while the market is closed. One narrow observation window is flagged across the projected 22:00-23:30 UTC futures reopen.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the weekend halt from Saturday evening through the hour before this one. The series was uniformly green with Tail fixed at 5, dominant mode normal, and Stress confined to a 25-28 band. Confidence decayed from 67 to 58 through the overnight hours as published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered steadily through 64, 72 and 80 to 83 as primary sources were re-verified on each hourly refresh. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next four projected hours remain inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 29 to 30 into the reopen and Confidence decays from 85 to 82. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen the conditional Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and far below the block threshold, covering the first live test of Friday's front-end repricing. It then eases through 11 and 10 across the Asian session to an overnight low of 8, lifts through 9 and 10 into a continental-only European morning thinned by the closed London market, and reaches a projected peak of 15 across the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open, where opening-auction imbalance meets month-end rebalancing on the final session of August. The window closes at 12 by U.S. early afternoon. Every projected hour maps to EA_ON and green; Stress peaks at 33 in the moderate band and Confidence declines gradually to 69.
